The chest CT scans showed ground-glass opacities (12 patients), sub pleural cysts (6 patients), and, less frequently, micronodules (2 patients), thickened interlobular septa (2 patients), honeycomb patterns (1 patient), and traction bronchiectasis (1 patient). A: Chest radiograph from a pediatric IPH case showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, a classic radiographic manifestation of idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis. The 'R' laterality marker is present as an annotation. B: Axial chest CT from the same IPH case showing diffuse bilateral symmetric alveolar infiltrates, consistent with the diffuse alveolar hemorrhage pattern of idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis. D: Histology panel with H&E and Prussian blue stains demonstrating hemosiderin-laden macrophages in alveolar spaces, the definitive histologic hallmark of idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis. Black arrows annotate the siderophages.

Chest CT indicated multiple exudative lesions in the right lung (Figure 3). The levels of CD19+ B cells and CD20+ B cells were 2.96% and 2.8%, respectively. Over a 6-month follow-up, prednisone was successfully tapered to 7.5 mg once daily without recurrent hemoptysis. By June 2026, hemoglobin levels normalized to 139 g/L (Figure 4).
